## 8. inventory vs inventoryNew

| file | rows | products | date min | date max | dup (product,date) | nulls | stock_received min/max | damaged_stock min/max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| inventory | 75,172 | 268 | 2023-03-17 | 2024-11-05 | 0 | 0 | 0/4 | 0/2 |
| inventoryNew | 18,105 | 268 | 2023-03-01 | 2024-11-01 | 12,534 | 0 | 1/4 | 0/7 |
- inventory is DAILY (dd-mm-yyyy); inventoryNew is MONTHLY (Mon-YY) with 1-6 rows per product-month (not unique).
- product-months: only in inventory 47, only in inventoryNew 0, both 5,571.
- on shared product-months: corr(received) 0.287, corr(damaged) 0.101; monthly received per product: inventory median 26 vs inventoryNew median 5.
- damaged_stock > stock_received: inventory 29,255 of 75,172 rows, inventoryNew 44 of 18,105.
- damage rate (damaged/received): inventory 54.41%, inventoryNew 3.85%.
- months covered: inventory 21, inventoryNew 21 (2023-03 to 2024-11).
- **Recommendation:** use `inventoryNew` (plausible damage rate, almost no damaged > received) aggregated to product x month, and drop `inventory` (damage rate above 50% and damaged > received on a large share of rows, i.e. an impossible state). Neither file has opening or closing stock and neither joins to orders by date or store, so inventory is an optional supply-quality page element (damage rate by category), not a stock-out analysis.

## 11. Signs the data is synthetic (read before trusting any insight)

Ratio of fullest to emptiest bin of a 10-bin histogram (about 1 = flat/uniform; real data is humped or skewed):

| variable | max/min bin ratio |
|---|---|
| orders.order_total | 184.00 |
| orders hour of day | 1.65 |
| orders day of week | 1.08 |
| delivery.distance_km | 1.18 |
| delivery.delivery_time_minutes | 12.60 |
| feedback.rating | 3.17 |
| products.price | 2.00 |
| marketing.impressions | 1.26 |
| marketing.roas | 1.13 |
| order_items.quantity | 1.04 |
| customers.total_orders | 1.23 |

- Monthly mean order_total ranges 2076 to 2329 (trend/seasonality check); corr(distance_km, delivery minutes) = 0.00; corr(rating, delay) = 0.00; corr(price, margin_percentage) = -0.06.
- Feedback text is 25 template sentences; every order has exactly one delivery row and one feedback row; order_items has one line per order; marketing revenue is 3x the orders table.

**Caveat to state on the report:** this is a synthetic/demo dataset. Relationships such as delay vs rating or spend vs revenue may be weak or absent by construction, so insights describe this data, not the real Blinkit.
